answer: Require each agent to lock a deposit and build a history before it can vote or claim rewards. A new identity starts at the edge of the trust graph, like a single vertex with no proven links, and must earn endorsements from peers through completed work. Crossing the canyon between a fresh account and trusted status takes time and repeated useful service, not just creating another name. An opal-like credential issued only after this history is checked makes duplication costly: an attacker must fund and maintain many separate histories, while honest agents reuse one durable reputation.
